_source.system: Link's inventory - the item id space, where inventory state lives in the save, what each item does, and how an item is granted.
_source.decomp: zeldaret/tww at Z:/memRip/sources/tww; every file:line below is relative to that root and was read directly.
_source.extends: Z:/memRip/knowledge/gamecube/projectile-items.md, which already covers Bow/arrows, Boomerang, Grappling Hook, Hookshot and Bombs in flight detail. This file does NOT repeat their physics; it covers ids, storage, the grant path, and the items that file does not cover.
_source.units: Frames are 30 fps. s16 angles: 0x10000 = 360 deg (0x4000 = 90 deg). Game-time is a f32 0..360 where 15.0 = 1 hour (d_kankyo.cpp:474).

_source.stub_warning: `/* Nonmatching */` in this repo has TWO meanings and you must look at the body to tell them apart. (a) The marker followed by an EMPTY body = the function is genuinely not decompiled; nothing near it is trustworthy. Verified example: src/d/d_menu_fmap.cpp:11-12 and every other function in that file. (b) The marker followed by a FULL body = decompiled but not byte-matching the original object; the code and its constants are real. Verified example: daShip_c::execute() at src/d/actor/d_a_ship.cpp:3545, whose ~1300-line body starts at :3546. See _stubbed_files for the audit.

_id_space.note: The enum is written as a single `enum ItemTable { ... }` with one entry per id 0x00..0xFF and an explicit /* 0xNN */ comment on every line; 0xFF is dItemNo_NONE_e (d_item_data.h:262). Ids are dense - there is no gap, unused slots are named dItemNo_NOENTRY_nn_e.

groups.0x00-0x1F: pickups / consumables (hearts, rupees, ammo, keys, fairy, Joy Pendant)
groups.0x20-0x34: the X/Y/Z inventory items (telescope .. Deku Leaf)
groups.0x35-0x36: bow upgrades (Fire/Ice arrows, Light arrows) - they overwrite the BOW inventory slot
groups.0x38-0x3E: swords and shields (equipment, not inventory slots)
groups.0x8C-0x9E: Delivery-Bag reserve items: flowers, flags, idols, letters, deeds
groups.0xAA-0xB8: Hurricane Spin, capacity upgrades, magic, Tingle rupees
groups.0xBF-0xFE: Treasure Charts / Sea Charts, numbered BACKWARDS: dItemNo_COLLECT_MAP_01_e is 0xFE and COLLECT_MAP_64_e is 0xBF

inventory_slots.meaning: mItems[slot] holds the dItemNo currently in that slot, or 0xFF for empty. The slot index is FIXED per item - the Deku Leaf is always slot 6 - so an item you do not have is simply 0xFF in its own slot.

slots.8: CAMERA (Picto Box or Deluxe Picto Box)
slots.12: BOW (also holds MAGIC_ARROW / LIGHT_ARROW once upgraded)

have_ever_flags.meaning: mItemFlags[inventorySlot] is a bit set. onItem(field, bit) sets bit `bit` of mItemFlags[field] (src/d/d_save.cpp:204-208). Bit 0 = 'you have the base item for this slot'; higher bits are UPGRADES for that slot.

known_bits.slot 2 (WIND_WAKER) bit 0: the Wind Waker (src/d/d_item.cpp:705). Note d_kankyo.cpp:519 gates the whole day/night clock on dComIfGs_isGetItem(2, 0) - time only passes once you own the baton.

_item_get.summary: Granting an item is always: (1) spawn a spinning item model actor tied to the demo, (2) play Link's ITEMGET animation and the get jingle, (3) show message 101 + itemNo, (4) when the item actor is deleted, its Delete() calls execItemGet(itemNo), which is the ONLY thing that actually writes the save.

grant_function.name: execItemGet(u8 itemNo)
grant_function.body: item_func_ptr[itemNo]() - a 256-entry table of void() functions, src/d/d_item.cpp:15-271
grant_function.shape: Each item_func_* is tiny and does exactly the save writes for that item. Canonical form for an inventory item: `dComIfGs_onGetItem(slot, bit); dComIfGs_setItem(slot, itemNo);` e.g. item_func_telescope (src/d/d_item.cpp:691-695).
grant_function.companion: checkItemGet(itemNo, defaultVal) -> item_getcheck_func_ptr[itemNo]() (src/d/d_item.cpp:539-546); returns -1 for 'no opinion', in which case defaultVal is used. Used by shops/NPCs to ask 'does Link already have this?'

spawn.fopAcM_createItemForPresentDemo: src/f_op/f_op_actor_mng.cpp:780-790 - asserts 0 <= itemNo < 256, records dComIfGp_event_setGtItm(itemNo), then fopAcM_createDemoItem(). Returns fpcM_ERROR_PROCESS_ID_e for itemNo 0xFF.
spawn.fopAcM_createItemForTrBoxDemo: src/f_op/f_op_actor_mng.cpp:793-803 - the treasure-chest variant, identical but argFlag 0.
spawn.actor: daDitem_c (fpcNm_Demo_Item_e), src/d/actor/d_a_demo_item.cpp. It looks up its model from dItem_data::item_resource[itemNo] (create(), d_a_demo_item.cpp:452-462), spins at +0x0111/frame around Y and billboards toward the camera unless FLAG_UNK02/04/08 is set (set_mtx(), 407-425).
spawn.the_write: daDitem_c::Delete() calls execItemGet(m_itemNo) UNLESS chkArgFlag(FLAG_UNK01) - src/d/actor/d_a_demo_item.cpp:437-441. FLAG_UNK01 therefore means 'display only, do not grant'; the Present demo (an NPC handing something over) uses it because the NPC's own script grants the item.
spawn.field_pickups: daItem_c (fpcNm_ITEM_e) in src/d/actor/d_a_item.cpp calls execItemGet(m_itemNo) directly at pickup (many sites, e.g. 591-763).

link_side.init: daPy_lk_c::dProcGetItem_init(), src/d/actor/d_a_player_dproc.inc:653-712. Plays ANM_ITEMGET (or first unequips whatever is in hand, mProcVar6=1). Spawns the item actor from mDemo.getParam0(); a param of 0x100 means 'use dComIfGp_event_getGtItm()' i.e. whatever the last createItemForPresentDemo announced (683-690). Calls dKy_Itemgetcol_chg_on() for the item-get lighting.
link_side.run: daPy_lk_c::dProcGetItem(), src/d/actor/d_a_player_dproc.inc:715-816. Timeline: frame < 10 keep re-reading the camera yaw; frame >= 11 start the jingle (setGetItemSound) and interpolate Link's facing to the camera over frames 10..17; when the animation ends, show() the item and open message MSG_NO_FOR_ITEM(itemNo); when the message closes, spin Link 180 degrees, cutEnd, item->dead().
link_side.heart_piece_special: itemNo 0x07 with (maxLife % 4) != 0 uses message HEART_PIECE_2/3/4 (0x17/0x18/0x19) instead, i.e. 'you have 2/3/4 pieces' - src/d/actor/d_a_player_dproc.inc:619-624 and the equivalent inline 0x7b + (maxLife%4) at 793-795.
link_side.jingle: daPy_lk_c::setGetItemSound(itemNo, isSmall), src/d/actor/d_a_player_dproc.inc:556-580. Rupees -> SE JA_SE_ME_ITEM_GET_S. Heart Container, or the 4th Heart Piece -> JA_BGM_GET_HEART. Heart Piece / Joy Pendant / Small Key / silver+orange rupee -> JA_BGM_ITEM_GET_S. Everything else -> the full JA_BGM_ITEM_GET fanfare.
link_side.present_variant: daPyProc_DEMO_PRESENT_e = 0xC3; dProcPresent_init_sub() (d_a_player_dproc.inc:1606-1625) plays ANM_PRESENTATIONA and spawns the item with FLAG_UNK01|FLAG_UNK02 so it is shown but not granted. Bottled items are skipped entirely (checkBottleItem).

cutscene_variant.how: STB cutscene command 5 carries a one-byte index into a static table `l_itemNo[]` and calls execItemGet(l_itemNo[argID]) directly - no item actor, no message.
cutscene_variant.note: Index 9 is dItemNo_NONE_e and grants nothing - the cutscene can say 'no item' without a separate opcode.

_wind_waker.player_code: src/d/actor/d_a_player_tact.inc (854 lines, fully decompiled, no stubs) - #included into d_a_player_main.cpp

procs.daPyProc_TACT_WAIT_e = 0x9A: holding the baton, conducting; reads the sticks each frame and judges the beat
procs.daPyProc_TACT_PLAY_e = 0x9B: a song was recognised - play the flourish animation and the melody
procs.daPyProc_TACT_PLAY_ORIGINAL_e = 0x9D: scripted free-form conducting during cutscenes (event supplies each stick pose)

conducting.controls: MAIN STICK = tempo/time signature, C-STICK = the note. mDoAud_getTactDirection(stick, prev) maps a stick to 0 neutral / 1 up / 2 right / 3 down / 4 left, with hysteresis: entering a direction needs |angle| > 0x6000 (up) or >= 0x2000 (right), leaving it needs > 0x7000 / 0x3000..0x5000, and the D-pad is accepted for the main stick when the stick is under 0.9 deflection (src/m_Do/m_Do_audio.cpp:204-256).
conducting.beat_from_main_stick: JAIZelInst::setBeat(dir): neutral(0) -> 3 beats @ 60 BPM, right(2) -> 6 beats @ 80 BPM, left(4) -> 4 beats @ 70 BPM. Anything else is ignored. (src/JAZelAudio/JAIZelInst.cpp:178-217)
conducting.note_frames: JAIZelInst::getMelodyGFrames: 30.0 / 25.714 / 22.5 frames per note, same scaling (src/JAZelAudio/JAIZelInst.cpp:456-470)
conducting.judging: daPy_lk_c::procTactWait counts m35A0 up to mDoAud_tact_getBeatFrames(), fires the metronome, waits 3 more frames (mProcVar0.m34D0 = 3) and then calls mDoAud_tact_judge(beatIndex, cStickDir) which appends the C-stick direction to a 6-entry ring and matches it against mMelodyPattern (src/d/actor/d_a_player_tact.inc:412-462; JAIZelInst::judge, src/JAZelAudio/JAIZelInst.cpp:299-395).
conducting.success: On a match the song must also be one you have learned - `dComIfGs_isTact(songIdx)` - and then a 30-frame delay (mProcVar1.m34D2 = 30) leads into procTactPlay_init (src/d/actor/d_a_player_tact.inc:463-469).
conducting.timeout: m35AC counts down one per frame from 900 frames (30 s), or 600 frames (20 s) for songs 6 and 7; hitting 0 cancels the baton (src/d/actor/d_a_player_tact.inc:283-287, 328-330).
conducting.arm_anims: right arm = the beat (ACTIONTAKTRUP / WAITTAKTRHANDL / ACTIONTAKTRDW / WAITTAKTRHANDR for dir 1/2/3/4), left arm = the note (WAITTAKTLHANDU/L/D/R). src/d/actor/d_a_player_tact.inc:64-88.
conducting.baton_tip: l_tact_top = (38.0, 7.5, 12.5) in the baton model's space; getTactTopPos() transforms it (src/d/actor/d_a_player_main_data.inc:27, d_a_player_tact.inc:128-136). The BRK on the baton is snapped to its last frame on every beat and back to 0 otherwise, which is the tip flash (d_a_player_tact.inc:427-437).
conducting.particles: ID_AK_JN_TAKT00 while conducting, ID_AK_JN_TAKT01 on a successful song (d_a_player_tact.inc:270, 519)

pattern_table.encoding: [0] = number of beats, [1..] = the C-stick direction for each beat, 0xFF = end. Directions: 0 = centre/neutral, 1 = up, 2 = right, 3 = down, 4 = left.
pattern_table.cross_check: d_msg.cpp:59 has the same beat counts as `const u8 mBeatNum[] = {3,4,4,6,6,3,3,4}` for the on-screen note guide.

songs.name: Wind's Requiem
songs.effect: Changes the global wind direction. procTactPlay checks dKyw_gbwind_use_check() - true only when the room's FILI GlobalWindLevel is <= 2 and no wind override is active (src/d/d_kankyo_wether.cpp:1406-1420). If allowed -> procTactPlayEnd_init(0), which ends the event camera and spawns fpcNm_WBIRD_e (src/d/actor/d_a_player_tact.inc:626-631, 682-684). Otherwise it prints message 0x14A5 ('the wind will not obey here').
songs.wind_picker: daWbird_c (src/d/actor/d_a_wbird.cpp) runs event 'TACT_WINDOW', calls dComIfGp_setOperateWindOn() to raise the 8-direction wheel, and on confirm flies off along the new wind; at its internal timer == 70 it calls dKyw_tact_wind_set_go() to commit the direction, and below 15 it zeroes the wind power for the gust (src/d/actor/d_a_wbird.cpp:104-113, 118-135). The wheel quantises to 45-degree steps: dOperate_wind_c::dOw_angleRegular returns 0/45/90/135/180/225/270/315 (src/d/d_operate_wind.cpp:57-79).
songs.storage: the chosen direction ends up in dSv_player_status_b_c::mTactWindAngleX/Y via dKyw_tact_wind_set (src/d/d_kankyo_wether.cpp:1329-1344)

songs.name: Ballad of Gales
songs.effect: Summons a cyclone that warps the ship. procTactPlay_init, if Link is on the ship AND the stage type is dStageType_SEA_e AND this is a normal (non-scripted) play, creates fpcNm_TORNADO_e with param 1 at Link's position and hands its id to the ship via ship->setTactWarpID() (src/d/actor/d_a_player_tact.inc:521-531). procTactPlay then only proceeds if that warp actor exists, otherwise message 0x14A6 (src/d/actor/d_a_player_tact.inc:632-638). procTactPlayEnd opens the sea chart with dComIfGp_fmapOpenOn() so you can pick a destination; if the ship reports getTactWarpPosNum() >= 0 it calls ship->setTactWarp(), else it cancels and deletes the tornado (src/d/actor/d_a_player_tact.inc:752-773).
songs.warp: daShip_c::procTactWarp lifts the ship up the tornado's joints and, once it is 5000 units above its start height, calls dStage_changeScene(mTactWarpPosNum + 0xC5, 0.0f, 0, 0xFF) - i.e. the cyclone destinations are spawn points 0xC5 + n (src/d/actor/d_a_ship.cpp:2847-2851).

songs.name: Command Melody
songs.effect: Take control of the partner NPC (Makar / Medli), or of a scripted object. procTactPlay requires checkNpcStatus() - a 'cb1' partner exists, has not refused (checkNpcNotChange), and is IN THE SAME ROOM as Link - and that Link is not on the ship; otherwise message 0x14A8 (src/d/actor/d_a_player_tact.inc:639-644; checkNpcStatus at 53-61). procTactPlayEnd_init(2) sets the talk partner to dComIfGp_getCb1Player() and orders event 'OPTION_CHAR_START' with SE JA_SE_CTRL_LINK_TO_NPC; when that event ends, changePlayer(cb1) actually swaps who you control (src/d/actor/d_a_player_tact.inc:686-691, 745-751).
songs.other_use: d_door.cpp:797 gates a door on dComIfGs_isTact(2), so the melody is also a plain 'do you know it' key.

songs.name: Earth God's Lyric
songs.effect: A DUET. It has no effect of its own in procTactPlay - it falls into the generic `else` that prints message 0x14A9 (src/d/actor/d_a_player_tact.inc:648-650). It only does something when an NPC has registered itself as the duet partner beforehand with daPy_lk_c::setTactZev(partnerId, expectedSongIndex, eventName) (src/d/actor/d_a_player_tact.inc:115-127). procTactPlay then checks mTactZevPartnerId != ERROR && m34CC == the song just played, and hands off to procTactPlayEnd_init(-1) which orders the partner's own event (src/d/actor/d_a_player_tact.inc:605-620, 674-679).
songs.in_game_meaning: sung with Medli to wake the Earth Sage; d_a_ship.cpp:463 also uses isTact(3)||isTact(4) as a story gate.

songs.name: Wind God's Aria
songs.effect: The other DUET - identical mechanism to the Earth God's Lyric (setTactZev partner path, generic message 0x14A9 otherwise). Sung with Makar to wake the Wind Sage. d_a_ship.cpp:450 checks isTact(4) as a story gate.

songs.name: Song of Passing
songs.effect: Flips day and night. procTactPlay first checks dKy_daynighttact_stop_chk() (an event has pinned the time, or mbDayNightTactStop) -> message 0x14A7; else if the room's FILI says dStage_FileList_dt_GetSongOk() it prints 0x14AA ('nothing happens here'); else procTactPlayEnd_init(5), which orders event 'TIMEWARP' (src/d/actor/d_a_player_tact.inc:645-655, 692-695).
songs.the_flip: When the TIMEWARP event ends, Link saves a turn-restart record (position, angle, room, getDayNightParamData(), plus the ship's position/angle and whether a ship exists) and calls dStage_turnRestart() (src/d/actor/d_a_player_tact.inc:713-741). dStage_turnRestart (src/d/d_stage.cpp:2375-2393) XORs the stage LAYER by 1, re-enters the same stage with start code -3, sets the next time to 0.0 (midnight) if it was daytime (hour 6..17) or 180.0 (noon) if it was night, and if the hour was 6..23 it advances the date and runs dKy_DayProc().

songs.name: unnamed melody 6
songs.effect: Not a learnable song - the judge explicitly excludes 6 and 7 from the isTact() check (src/d/actor/d_a_player_tact.inc:465), and its baton timeout is 600 frames instead of 900 (d_a_player_tact.inc:283-287). Used only when an event forces a specific song index. Which cutscene uses it: NOT DETERMINED.

songs.name: unnamed melody 7
songs.effect: same as melody 6 - event-only. NOT DETERMINED which one.

TELESCOPE.name: Telescope
TELESCOPE.behaviour: Grant is `onGetItem(slot 0, bit 0); setItem(slot 0, 0x20)`. Taking it out only builds the model (dRes_INDEX_LINK_BDL_TELESCOPE_e); the actual first-person view is daPyProc_SCOPE_e = 0x00.

TINGLE_TUNER.name: Tingle Tuner
TINGLE_TUNER.behaviour: Selecting it does NOT take out an item - checkNewItemChange routes it to `fopAcM_orderTalkEvent(this, dComIfGp_getAgb())`, i.e. it starts a conversation with the AGB (GBA-link) actor (src/d/actor/d_a_player_main.cpp:3798-3799). Link's own state is daPyProc_DEMO_AGB_USE_e = 0xCA (include/d/actor/d_a_player_main.h:619).
TINGLE_TUNER.implementing_files: ALL REAL, zero empty stubs: src/d/actor/d_a_agb.cpp (1877 lines, header comment 'Tingle Tuner Cursor / AGB Cursor', profile g_profile_AGB / fpcNm_AGB_e at :1866) is the on-screen Tingle cursor; src/d/actor/d_a_agbsw0.cpp (2600 lines) is the hint / bomb-spawning / statue / item-buy logic; src/m_Do/m_Do_gba_com.cpp (722 lines) is the GC-to-GBA link layer; src/JSystem/JUtility/JUTGba.cpp (404 lines) is the JUTGba manager; src/dolphin/gba/*.c (GBA.c, GBAJoyBoot.c, GBARead.c, GBAWrite.c, GBAXfer.c, GBAGetProcessStatus.c) is the SDK transport.
TINGLE_TUNER.boot_flow: d_a_agb.cpp:599-616 uploadFuncTable[] = uploadInitCheck, uploadPortCheckWait, uploadSelect, uploadJoyboot1, uploadJoyboot2, uploadConnect, uploadMessageLoad, uploadMessageLoad2, uploadMessageSend, [uploadRetryWait on non-JP], uploadMsgEndWait, uploadMsgEndTimer, driven by modeLoad() (:625-636). The GBA client binary is DVD-loaded per region as /res/Gba/client_u.bin (USA) or client_<lang>.bin (PAL) (:400-409). uploadJoyboot1 calls JUTGba::doJoyBoot(port, 3, -1, program, size-4, NULL, NULL) with a 450-frame timeout (:424-436); uploadJoyboot2 polls resultJoyBoot and on failure shows message 7 'An error has occurred.' (:439-505). The actor is created once per scene at src/d/d_stage.cpp:1497-1498, object name 'Agb' (:1237).
TINGLE_TUNER.reads_links_progress: d_a_agb.cpp:1209 reads dComIfGs_isTact(0); d_a_agbsw0.cpp:1017-1022 reads isCollect(2,0) / isTact(1); :908-916 gates hints on checkGetItem(BAIT_BAG) and checkBaitItem(HYOI_PEAR); :2247 reads checkGetItem(IRON_BOOTS). It can also GIVE things: d_a_agb.cpp:1102 calls dComIfGs_setBaitItem(dItemNo_BIRD_BAIT_5_e).
TINGLE_TUNER.implementation_note: The whole point of the item is a second screen driven by a second player. For a remake the honest options are to cut it, or to reimplement its effects (bombs, rupees, hints, Tingle statues) as an in-game menu. The GAMEPLAY side is fully recoverable - d_a_agbsw0.cpp is 2600 lines of real code - but the GBA transport is not worth porting. This pass established only the entry point and the boot flow.

WIND_WAKER.name: Wind Waker (Tact)
WIND_WAKER.file: src/d/actor/d_a_player_tact.inc; src/JAZelAudio/JAIZelInst.cpp; src/d/d_metronome.cpp (the on-screen beat guide); src/d/d_msg.cpp (the note guide)
WIND_WAKER.behaviour: See the whole _wind_waker section. Take-out is special: setTactModel() clears mEquipItem first (src/d/actor/d_a_player_main.cpp:3719-3722) and loads dRes_INDEX_LINK_BDL_TAKT_e plus BRK TTAKT for the tip flash (d_a_player_tact.inc:33-49). Conducting sets daPyStts1_WIND_WAKER_CONDUCT_e (d_a_player_tact.inc:255).
WIND_WAKER.implementation_note: Not yet in the remake. Build it as: an input reader mapping both sticks to 0..4 with the hysteresis constants; a metronome ticking at beat_frames; a ring buffer of C-stick directions judged 3 frames after each beat; a table lookup against pattern_table.raw gated by the learned-song bits; then a per-song effect handler. The wind, the day/night flip and the cyclone warp are all just save writes plus a scene reload, so they are cheap; Command Melody needs a partner-NPC swap.

PICTO_BOX.name: Picto Box
PICTO_BOX.behaviour: Grant is onGetItem(slot 8, bit 0) + setItem(slot 8, 0x23). The Picto Box and the Deluxe share slot 8 and the same model - setPhotoBoxModel() loads dRes_INDEX_LINK_BDL_CAMERA_e and HIDES the joint CAMERA_JNT_FRASH_e for the plain box, SHOWS it for the Deluxe (src/d/actor/d_a_player_main.cpp:3747-3761). daPy_lk_c::checkPhotoBoxItem(itemNo) is simply `itemNo == PICTO_BOX || itemNo == DELUXE_PICTO_BOX` (src/d/actor/d_a_player_main.cpp:5647-5649). Held pictograph count lives in dSv_player_item_record2_c::mPictureNum (include/d/d_save.h:145).
PICTO_BOX.aiming: It reuses the TELESCOPE proc. Pressing R with it equipped calls procScope_init(mEquipItem) -> daPyProc_SCOPE_e = 0x00 (src/d/actor/d_a_player_main.cpp:4085-4086, 4247-4248), which sets daPyStts1_PICTO_BOX_AIM_e (0x00000008) rather than daPyStts0_TELESCOPE_LOOK_e (:5904-5917; flag include/d/d_com_inf_game.h:83). The camera mirrors it with dCamAttnStts_PICTO_BOX_AIM_e = 0x40 (include/d/d_com_inf_game.h:109; src/d/d_camera.cpp:3976, 4000, 4173). Cancelling raises daPyFlg0_PHOTO_BOX_CANCEL = 0x00080000 (include/d/actor/d_a_player.h:184).
PICTO_BOX.capacity: THREE pictographs, hard-coded as `< 3` at three sites: the shutter is only allowed when mDoGph_getCaptureStep()==0 && getPictureNum() < 3 (src/d/d_picture_box.cpp:650), the 'take photo' prompt is only shown while < 3 (:1020-1025), and Lenzo refuses the Legendary Pictograph unless < 3 (src/d/actor/d_a_npc_photo.cpp:1743, 2141). In memory it is card_pictdata* mPhotoBuffer[4] - 'three saved slots plus one import/get temporary slot' (include/d/d_picture_box.h:166).
PICTO_BOX.capture: dJle_Pb_c::cameraMode(), src/d/d_picture_box.cpp:653-660: the PLAIN Picto Box captures GX_TF_I8 (8-bit intensity = black and white), the DELUXE captures GX_TF_RGB565 (colour); both are then re-encoded to GX_TF_CMPR for storage, and the chosen format is saved per photo in card_pictdata::capture_format (:610) and restored on browse (:826). Resolution 152 x 104 (src/m_Do/m_Do_graphic.cpp:838-839); the saved blob is a 0x2000-byte card_pictdata with u8 tex_buffer[0x1EE0] holding one 152x104 CMPR texture (include/m_Do/m_Do_MemCardRWmng.h:19-27).
PICTO_BOX.judging: src/d/d_snap.cpp (2257 lines, fully real). dSnap_packet::m_judge_tbl has 11 entries (:16-31): JudgePost, JudgeBikutsuki, JudgeCoupleLook, JudgeGF, JudgeGenzo, JudgeObasan4/JudgeGene (version-dependent), JudgeGene x3, JudgeTestM. Per-subject framing rules are in `static const CharaData l_CharaData[]` (struct :34-44, table from :45) with fields offset / radius / height / minRatio / cullAngle / minPixels / figRoom; entry 0 is offset (0,10,0), radius 25, height 80, minRatio 500, cullAngle 0x2000, minPixels 5000, figRoom 0x03 (:46-56).
PICTO_BOX.implementation_note: Render-to-texture into a 152x104 buffer, three save slots, greyscale for the plain box and colour for the Deluxe, plus a judging pass that scores the framing of a tagged subject (distance, on-screen pixel count, view angle). Note the annotated RETAIL BUG: dPb_erasePicture() decrements the count and sets an event-reg bit but never clears the picture flags, so deleted photos are never removed from the memory card (fixed for PAL) - src/d/d_picture_box.cpp:44-59.

DELUXE_PICTO_BOX.name: Deluxe Picto Box
DELUXE_PICTO_BOX.behaviour: Grant is `onGetItem(slot 8, bit 1); setItem(slot 8, 0x26)` - it REPLACES the Picto Box in the same slot but sets a second bit so the save still knows you once had the plain one. Two mechanical differences: the model's flash joint CAMERA_JNT_FRASH_e is SHOWN (src/d/actor/d_a_player_main.cpp:3747-3756), and cameraMode() captures GX_TF_RGB565 instead of GX_TF_I8 - i.e. colour instead of black and white (src/d/d_picture_box.cpp:653-660).
DELUXE_PICTO_BOX.how_obtained: Give Lenzo the Firefly bottle once his event register is >= 6 and you do not already have it: he empties the bottle and awards dItemNo_DELUXE_PICTO_BOX_e (src/d/actor/d_a_npc_photo.cpp:1749-1755). Handing him the Deluxe box back while temp bit UNK_0302 is set buys a LEGENDARY_PICTOGRAPH if getPictureNum() < 3, else message 0x3787 (:1742-1748).
DELUXE_PICTO_BOX.implementation_note: Same system as the Picto Box with colour output. The 7 Legendary Pictographs are pre-authored images shipped on the disc, imported as CMPR into a photo slot - not something the camera takes.

SPOILS_BAG.name: Spoils Bag
SPOILS_BAG.behaviour: Grant is onGetItem(slot 4, bit 0) + setItem(slot 4, 0x24). Contents live in dSv_player_bag_item_c::mBeast[8] with counts in mBagItemRecord.mBeastNum[8] and a have-ever bitmask in mGetBagItem.mBeastFlags. Each spoil has a fixed index (dBeastIdx_e, include/d/d_com_inf_game.h:1277-1285) and its item_func is the same three lines every time, e.g. item_func_skull_necklace: setBeastItem(0x45); onGetItemBeast(0); setItemBeastNumCount(0, 1) (src/d/d_item.cpp:904-909).
SPOILS_BAG.implementation_note: A simple 8-slot counted inventory. The per-slot maximum is NOT stated in the save code (mBeastNum is a plain u8); see _not_determined.

BAIT_BAG.name: Bait Bag
BAIT_BAG.behaviour: Grant is onGetItem(slot 11, bit 0) + setItem(slot 11, 0x2C). Contents in mBagItem.mBait[8]. USING a bait does not equip a model - checkNewItemChange sends `isEsa(itemNo)` straight into a player proc: dItemNo_HYOI_PEAR_e (0x83) -> procFoodSet_init() (daPyProc_FOOD_SET_e = 0xA8), any other bait -> procFoodThrow_init() (daPyProc_FOOD_THROW_e = 0xA7). Both require Link to be on the ground and not flying (src/d/actor/d_a_player_main.cpp:3785-3797).
BAIT_BAG.implementation_note: Two distinct verbs: throw (feed a fish) and set-on-head (Hyoi Pear -> a seagull carries the camera). Both start from the item menu, not from a held item.

DELIVERY_BAG.name: Delivery Bag
DELIVERY_BAG.behaviour: Grant is onGetItem(slot 18, bit 0) + setItem(slot 18, 0x30). Contents live in mBagItem.mReserve[8] with counts mReserveNum[8] and a 32-bit have-ever mask mGetBagItem.mReserveFlags (the only bag with 32 bits, because it holds far more than 8 distinct item types over a playthrough). Reserve is the only bag with an `offReserve` - items are consumed when delivered (src/d/d_save.cpp:705-710). Selecting a reserve item (ids 0x98 FATHER_LETTER .. 0x9E FILL_UP_COUPON) goes through checkNewItemChange to procNotUse_init(itemNo) unless something else claims it (src/d/actor/d_a_player_main.cpp:3788, 3818-3821).
DELIVERY_BAG.implementation_note: Delivery is driven by the receiving NPCs (they check dComIfGs_checkReserveItem and call offReserve), not by the bag. d_a_dai.cpp:123 shows the pattern: `if (!checkItemGet(dItemNo_DELIVERY_BAG_e, TRUE))`.

POWER_BRACELETS.name: Power Bracelets
POWER_BRACELETS.behaviour: NOT an inventory slot. Grant is `dComIfGs_onCollect(2, 0); dComIfGs_setSelectEquip(2, 0x28)` - it sets bit 0 of dSv_player_collect_c::mCollect[2] and writes the item number into dSv_player_status_a_c::mSelectEquip[2]. Possession is tested with dComIfGs_isCollect(0x2, 0) (src/d/d_item.cpp:2186). Once owned it is always on; there is no equip/unequip.
POWER_BRACELETS.implementation_note: Model it as a boolean capability flag consulted by liftable objects, not an item. dItemNo_BARE_HAND_e (0x2E) writes the same mSelectEquip[2] slot with a 'no bracelet' value (src/d/d_item.cpp:775-778), so the game can take them away.

IRON_BOOTS.name: Iron Boots
IRON_BOOTS.behaviour: Grant is onGetItem(slot 9, bit 0) + setItem(slot 9, 0x29). Selecting them from a button does NOT take out an item: checkNewItemChange requires Link to be ON THE GROUND and not flying, then calls procBootsEquip_init(itemNo) - daPyProc_BOOTS_EQUIP_e = 0xA1 (src/d/actor/d_a_player_main.cpp:3790-3791; include/d/actor/d_a_player_main.h:577). They are a toggle: pressing the same button again while checkEquipHeavyBoots() is true re-enters procBootsEquip_init to take them off (src/d/actor/d_a_player_main.cpp:3871-3872). The worn state is the player flag daPyFlg0_EQUIP_HEAVY_BOOTS, NOT the inventory slot; checkEquipHeavyBoots() = checkNoResetFlg0(daPyFlg0_EQUIP_HEAVY_BOOTS) (include/d/actor/d_a_player.h:539). The flag actually flips at ANIMATION FRAME 11.0 of ANM_SETBOOTS (src/d/actor/d_a_player_main.cpp:8468-8474), with a rumble StartShock(5, -0x31, (0,1,0)) at frame 15.0 (:8499-8501). Safety nets: the flag is cleared every frame if no X/Y/Z button still holds the Iron Boots (:11229-11234), and UNCONDITIONALLY on entering water (src/d/actor/d_a_player_swim.inc:129).

effects.gravity: checkHeavyStateOn() -> speed.y += gravity * 2.25 and the fall-speed floor becomes maxFallSpeed * 1.5 (src/d/actor/d_a_player_main.cpp:2464-2472)
effects.movement: mStickDistance is halved (*0.5) at src/d/actor/d_a_player_main.cpp:10636, so top speed, acceleration (:2816) and the DoStatus threshold (:2182) all scale by 0.5, while the turn rate is scaled by 1/(0.5*0.5) = 4x (:2757). Rolls are also *0.5 (:6810, :6818, :6954).
effects.animation: swaps to ANM_WALKHBOOTS / ANM_WALKHBOOTSKAZE (leaning into wind) with anim rate 0.85 and blend 0.7 (src/d/actor/d_a_player_main.cpp:2983-3010)
effects.wind: THE HEADLINE MECHANIC. setWindAtPower() zeroes the positional wind push while heavy: `m3730.x = m3730.z = 0.0f` (src/d/actor/d_a_player_main.cpp:11128-11133). m3730 is what actually displaces Link (:2589-2590). The lean accumulator m373C still builds, so Link still leans - he just does not slide. Un-booted, the wind push magnitude is clamped to 27.0 (or 30.0 for non-special wind) (:11099-11112).
effects.deku_leaf: heavy state blocks gliding entirely - no magic spent, no glide, and the glide gravity override is skipped (src/d/actor/d_a_player_fan.inc:357-359, 385-395, 411, 444, 482-484)
effects.water: THERE IS NO SINKING. Unlike Ocarina of Time, the boots are simply removed on water entry (src/d/actor/d_a_player_swim.inc:129).
effects.objects: read by heavy floor switches and pushable/jumpable objects via checkEquipHeavyBoots(): src/d/actor/d_a_floor.cpp:21,23; d_a_obj_swheavy.cpp:211; d_a_obj_swpush.cpp:369; d_a_obj_jump.cpp:255; d_a_obj_homen.cpp:519, 806

equip_anim_hio.file: src/d/actor/d_a_player_HIO_data.inc:271-273 (daPy_HIO_boots_c0::m); used as setSingleMoveAnime(ANM_SETBOOTS, 1.0, 0.0, 19, 5.0) at src/d/actor/d_a_player_main.cpp:8454-8460, and 19.0 is the frame after which checkNextMode(1) may interrupt (:8486)

IRON_BOOTS.implementation_note: A toggled movement mode: halve stick magnitude, quadruple turn rate, 2.25x gravity with a 1.5x terminal, immunity to wind displacement, no gliding, swap the walk animation, and set a 'heavy' collision tag that heavy floor switches look for. Toggle only on the ground; force off on water entry and whenever the item leaves the buttons.

MAGIC_ARMOR.name: Magic Armor
MAGIC_ARMOR.behaviour: Grant is onGetItem(slot 10, bit 0) + setItem(slot 10, 0x2A). Selecting it is handled BEFORE the ground check, at the very top of checkNewItemChange: `if (itemNo == dItemNo_MAGIC_ARMOR_e) return changeDragonShield(1);` (src/d/actor/d_a_player_main.cpp:3782-3783) - so unlike the Iron Boots it can be switched on IN MID-AIR. Its state is the player flag daPyFlg1_EQUIP_DRAGON_SHIELD ('dragon shield' is the internal name; the get-model archive is VmagS); checkEquipDragonShield() = checkNoResetFlg1(daPyFlg1_EQUIP_DRAGON_SHIELD) (include/d/actor/d_a_player.h:550). Pressing the button again clears the flag (src/d/actor/d_a_player_main.cpp:3868-3869); it is also cleared if no button holds it (:11235-11240) and on entering water (src/d/actor/d_a_player_swim.inc:130). It survives a scene load via bit 0x8000 of lastMode (src/d/d_com_inf_game.cpp:673-675).

magic_drain.activation: changeDragonShield() refuses with SE JA_SE_ITEM_TARGET_OUT if magic is 0; otherwise it sets the flag, seeds the countdown m3548 = 60, and spends 1 MP immediately (src/d/actor/d_a_player_main.cpp:3765-3771)
magic_drain.per_frame: m3548 -= 1 each frame but NOT while an event is running; at 0 it spends another 1 MP and reloads 60, and if magic has run out it clears the flag instead (src/d/actor/d_a_player_particle.inc:500-515)
magic_drain.rate: 1 MP on activation, then 1 MP every 60 frames

damage_nullification.effect: setDamagePoint() takes the else branch: dComIfGp_setItemLifeCount is never called and SE JA_SE_LK_MGC_SHIELD_DEF plays instead - damage is FULLY nullified, not reduced (src/d/actor/d_a_player_main.cpp:4982-4999). Because the offNoResetFlg1(daPyFlg1_SOUP_POWER_UP) lines live in the damaging branch, the armour also protects the Soup buff.
damage_nullification.other_sites: fatal-damage check (:5006), drowning (:5171), ship ride (:5200), ReDead grab (src/d/actor/d_a_rd.cpp:1115), src/d/actor/d_a_ship.cpp:1202

aura_brk.value: BRK_YAURA00_R / BRK_YMGCS00_MS (red; the green pair is the Tingle Shield)

MAGIC_ARMOR.implementation_note: A toggle with a 60-frame MP tick and a boolean 'ignore all damage' predicate consulted at the top of the damage path. Toggleable in mid-air; must auto-disable at 0 magic and be force-disabled on water entry. Add a red aura and a magic-meter flash (src/d/d_meter.cpp:4326).

SKULL_HAMMER.name: Skull Hammer
SKULL_HAMMER.file: src/d/d_item.cpp:804-808 (grant); src/d/actor/d_a_player_hammer.inc (411 lines, fully decompiled); src/d/actor/d_a_obj_swhammer.cpp (the hammer pegs)

wind_physics.where: daShip_c::procSteerMove(), src/d/actor/d_a_ship.cpp:1621-1719 (this function is matching real code; only daShip_c::execute() carries a Nonmatching marker, and it has a full body)
wind_physics.formula: windPower = |wind| / 0.5, clamped to 1.0; angleDiff = |windAngle - ship yaw|; windFactor = (angleDiff < 0x4000) ? 1.0 - angleDiff/0x10000 : (angleDiff <= 0x6000) ? 0.75 - (angleDiff-0x4000)*5.493164e-05 : max(0, 0.3 - (angleDiff-0x6000)*0.00032967035); then windPower *= windFactor * 55.0 (src/d/actor/d_a_ship.cpp:1634-1653)
wind_physics.curve: dead-on tailwind factor 1.0; 90 deg off (0x4000) 0.75; 135 deg (0x6000) 0.30; ~157.5 deg and beyond 0.0
wind_physics.ramp_up: on the frame the sail catches (7.0) speedF snaps to windPower * 2.0 clamped to 80.0 (:1656-1659); afterwards cLib_addCalc(&speedF, windPower, 0.1, 0.5, 0.1) (:1677), or decrementShipSpeed() if already faster (:1675)
wind_physics.no_sail: with the sail down, speed chases mStickMVal * 10.0 * cos(mStickMAng) (:1673)
wind_physics.jump: the wave-ramp jump needs mFwdVel > 16.5 and windPower >= 11.0; R sets speed.y = windPower clamped to [15.0, 40.0] and mJumpRate = (speed.y - 11.0) * 0.014545455 (:1686-1699)
wind_physics.boom_angle: setSailAngle() targets +/-0x1555 (~30 deg) by the sign of windAngle - ship yaw with a +/-0x800 deadzone, eased with cLib_addCalcAngleS(..., 0x10, 0x800, 0x20) (src/d/actor/d_a_ship.cpp:758-794, applied :116-117)

SAIL.implementation_note: The remake already sails. Two things to get right: (1) sail thrust must read the SAME wind vector that the Wind's Requiem writes, so changing the wind actually changes sailing; (2) copy the three-segment windFactor curve verbatim - the 1.0 / 0.75 / 0.30 / 0.0 breakpoints at 0, 90, 135 and ~157 degrees are what makes tacking feel right.

TRIFORCE_CHART.behaviour: WARNING: every item_func_triforce_mapN is an EMPTY FUNCTION (src/d/d_item.cpp:1126-1157). How many hearts a Red Potion gives, how much magic a Green Potion gives, what Blue Potion and Soup restore, and how the fairy auto-revive works, are all inside d_a_player_bottle.inc's drink/open procs and were NOT read. Only the Forest Water timer (36000 frames) was confirmed.
Picto Box capacity. mPictureNum exists in the save (include/d/d_save.h:145) but I did not find the constant that caps it, nor the colour/black-and-white switch inside d_picture_box.cpp / d_snap.cpp.

Per-slot maximum for bag items. mBeastNum[8] / mBaitNum[8] / mReserveNum[8] are plain u8 arrays and d_save.cpp does not clamp them; a cap (if any) must be in the setItemBeastNumCount / dComIfGp_setItem*NumCount helpers, which I did not read.

Melodies 6 and 7. They have real conducting patterns (up/down/right and up/right/left/down) and a shorter 600-frame timeout, but they are excluded from the isTact() learned-song check, so they are event-only. Which cutscenes drive them is unknown.

The free-play recogniser. JAIZelInst::m_note_pattern[6][6] and m_stick_to_note_table[25] are real data, but I could not establish what consumes setStickPos()'s return value in gameplay, so do NOT assume those six entries are the six songs.

Ballad of Gales destinations. dStage_changeScene(mTactWarpPosNum + 0xC5, ...) is real, but NOTHING in the decompiled source ever calls setTactWarpPosNum - the caller is in src/d/d_menu_fmap.cpp, which is 131 /* Nonmatching */ stubs in 669 lines, i.e. essentially entirely undecompiled. The mapping from a cyclone icon on the sea chart to a spawn-point index is therefore not recoverable from this decomp.

The wind-direction wheel. dOperate_wind_c::windSet(), arrowDirection(), initialize(), _create() and 19 other functions in src/d/d_operate_wind.cpp are /* Nonmatching */ (23 of ~25 functions). Only dOw_angleRegular (8 directions at 45 degrees, src/d/d_operate_wind.cpp:57-79) and dOw_stickControl are real. The exact s16 angle written for each of the 8 compass directions was NOT recovered; dKyw_tact_wind_set(x, y) is the setter to feed.

Tingle Tuner gameplay. d_a_agb.cpp (1877 lines) and d_a_agbsw0.cpp are real decompiled code, so its features ARE recoverable, but mining them was out of scope here. All I established is the entry point (orderTalkEvent with the AGB actor) and the state daPyProc_DEMO_AGB_USE_e.
Hurricane Spin (0xAA): id only; no behaviour established.
dSv_player_item_record_c::mBottleNum[3] and dSv_player_status_a_c::mSelectEquip[3]: both exist and are initialised, but I found no reader for either.
